extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament, policymakers, and the informed British public concerned with East India Company governance and colonial finance
extracted.subtask_description: A parliamentary/pamphlet‑style critique evaluating the legitimacy of private claims on public/colonial revenues and the conduct of East India Company servants and ministers in contracting and securing those debts. Focuses on standards of evidence, authority, transparency, conflict of interest, and legal safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debt requires an equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every debt, for which an equivalent of some kind or other is not given, is, on the face of it, a fraud."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legitimate claim demanding public payment must be supported by an identifiable equivalent (property, revenue, contractual right). If no equivalent exists or is shown, the claim should be treated as fraudulent and not supported by government or public funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government should not interpose for claims that defy its authority
rubrics_metrics.description: It was not necessary that the authority of government should interpose in favor of claims whose very foundation was a defiance of that authority, and whose object and end was its entire subversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public authorities must refuse to enforce or subsidize private claims that undermine public authority or were created in contempt of legal or administrative limits; such disputes should remain between the private parties unless proven lawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior knowledge and approbation of directors required for validity
rubrics_metrics.description: This debt was never contracted with the knowledge of the Company; that it had not their approbation; that they received the first intelligence of it with the utmost possible surprise, indignation, and alarm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debts or assignments executed by company servants require prior, documented knowledge and explicit approval by the governing board; absence of such approval undermines the transaction's legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial inquiry and accountability for breaches of trust
rubrics_metrics.description: "We order and direct that you do examine, in the most impartial manner, all the above-mentioned transactions, and that you punish, by suspension, degradation, dismission, or otherwise... all and every such servant or servants of the Company who may by you be found guilty of any of the above offences."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of misconduct in contracting debts require a full, impartial investigation and proportionate disciplinary or legal sanctions for servants found guilty (suspension, degradation, dismissal, prosecution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Servants must prefer public/company interest over private gain
rubrics_metrics.description: The servants of the Company ... have, in this instance most unfaithfully betrayed their trust, abandoned the Company's interest, and prostituted its influence to accomplish the purposes of individuals, whilst the interest of the Company is almost wholly neglected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials and agents owe a fiduciary duty to prioritize the corporation's or public interest; transactions that advance private parties at the expense of the public trust are disqualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexplained rapid accumulation of wealth indicates illegitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: "How can you or I account for such immense fortunes acquired in so short a time, without any visible means of getting them?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sudden large fortunes by servants or intermediaries dealing with public/colonial revenues should trigger scrutiny for fraud, bribery, or abusive practices; lack of visible lawful sources is suspicious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and transparent disclosure to oversight bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: It was two years before the Court of Directors obtained any official intelligence of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactions affecting public revenues or sovereignty require prompt, full reporting to the appropriate oversight body; significant delays in disclosure frustrate accountability and invalidate claims of proper sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest: officials must not act as creditors/agents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presidency did approve the debt is certain. But ... the Presidency were the very persons guilty of contracting this loan,--creditors themselves, and agents and trustees for all the other creditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials must not directly serve as creditors, agents, or trustees for private claims against the public they administer; such dual roles create self‑interest and corrupt decision‑making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assignment of territorial revenue to private creditors
rubrics_metrics.description: An express clause immediately preceded, positively forbidding any British subject from receiving assignments upon any part of the territorial revenue, on any pretence whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal or statutory provisions that bar assigning public/territorial revenues to private parties should be respected; removal or circumvention of such clauses enables predatory appropriation of public income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent usurious compounding and opaque interest practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The first interest paid was from thirty to thirty-six per cent; it was then brought down to twenty-five per cent; at length it was reduced to twenty ... as often as any of these monstrous interests fell into an arrear, the arrear, formed into a new capital, was added to the old, and the same interest of twenty per cent accrued upon both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest rates and mechanisms must be transparent and just; converting arrears into new principal and retroactively piling high interest creates unjust, usurious obligations that should not be recognized or enforced by public authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not allow concentration of private creditor influence to subvert corporate governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The private creditors instantly qualified a vast number of votes; and having made themselves masters of the Court of Proprietors ... they so completely overturned the authority of the Court of Directors at home and abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting private claimants to acquire disproportionate voting or political influence to override oversight bodies is corrosive of governance and should be prevented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting integrity: do not record or treat non‑cash as cash
rubrics_metrics.description: "The banker engages to pay the money, and grants his notes accordingly, which he puts in the cash-book as ready money... By this means not a cash is advanced by the banker, though he receives a heavy interest from the Nabob..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial books must not record fictitious cash advances; representing credit instruments or promises as actual cash inflows to disguise lack of funds is fraudulent and invalidates subsequent claims based on such entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on the debtor's personal faith as security for public sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company had actually given it their sanction, though always relying for its validity on the sole security of the faith of him who without their knowledge or consent entered into the original obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public sanction of claims that rests only on a ruler's or debtor's personal promise (without legal assignment, revenue security, or board approval) is insufficient; institutional or legal security must back public liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve legal safeguards; oppose retroactive removal of protections
rubrics_metrics.description: An express clause ... forbidding any British subject from receiving assignments ... The Chancellor ... expunged this essential clause, broke down the fence which was raised to cover the public property against the rapacity of his partisans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative or regulatory safeguards that protect public property and revenues should not be repealed or weakened to accommodate partisan or private interests; doing so invites systemic abuse.
